mission: Answer 'would PERFECT paddle ownership eliminate the F09 residual?' by feeding ground-truth ownership (fixture construction + dual-labeled ownership set) into estimateContact in place of current paddle track selection, and quantifying (a) current ownership accuracy, (b) oracle ownership, (c) downstream contact error / confident-wrong rate under each, on all adversarial contact fixtures plus every replayable committed contact gold case.

method.ownershipAccuracy: packages/swing-lab ownershipBench runBench(includeHeldOut=false, applyCorrections=true), incumbent_wrist_ratio method, source-session grouping preserved
method.adversarialFixtures: All 10 generated adversarial contact fixtures (packages/evaluation adversarialContactFixtures) plus exact reconstructions of the e09 F2 (foreign paddle beyond reach) and F3 (foreign paddle within reach) red-team scenarios from packages/vision-geometry/test/contactRedTeam.test.ts. 'current' = paddle tracks as constructed (incl. foreign); 'oracle' = ground-truth ownership by construction (foreign paddle tracks removed; target-owned tracks kept).
method.committedGold: Every replayable committed contact gold event via the same loader/geometry as packages/vision-geometry/eval/contactGoldReplay.ts (verified row-identical to canonical replayAll() under the current_no_paddle condition). Three ownership conditions per event: current_no_paddle (production behavior: no paddle track fed), oracle_ownership (target-labeled paddle annotation points fed as paddleCenters, speeds derived when >=2 in-window points), wrong_ownership (adversarial control: other-player paddle points fed as if target-owned).
method.thresholds: strict=66ms, acceptable=132ms, confident-wrong = confidence>=0.7 AND error>132ms (fixtures: >=0.6 AND error>150ms matching contactRedTeam constants); estimator = contact-evidence-4.3 at integration head, Linux replay (non-canonical; no Mac/Apple Vision cascade, no Mac/iPhone numbers claimed)

committedGoldEvents.grouping: by source bundle/session, no random frame splits

holdoutStatement: Held-out cases wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 were never read, listed, touched, or referenced; the committed-gold loader and ownership bench exclude them by construction (includeHeldOut=false).

configuration.oracleOwnershipDefinition: gold label itself: 100% correct by construction, not a measurement

measuredResults.b_oracleOwnership: 100% by construction (ground-truth labels; not a measurement)

c_adversarialFixtures.f3Detail: F3 (foreign-paddle-within-reach): current = confident modality-confirmed wrong (error 590ms, confidence 0.778). Oracle ownership (foreign track removed) = ABSTAIN with multi-modal reason (clusters ~1715ms vs ~1100ms, 98% as strong). Perfect ownership eliminates the confident-wrong commitment but does NOT recover a correct estimate: the ball-turn decoy near the idle target wrist keeps the evidence ambiguous.

paddlePointAvailability.note: committed paddle annotations are sparse (1-10 points per event window), far below a dense track

findings: F3 synthetic residual IS upstream-attributable: with perfect ownership (foreign paddle removed) the confident modality-confirmed wrong marker (error 590ms, confidence 0.778) becomes an honest multi-modal abstention. Confident-wrong across 12 fixtures: 1 (current) -> 0 (oracle).

Perfect ownership does NOT fully solve F3: the estimator abstains rather than localizing the true contact, because the ball-turn decoy near the idle target wrist survives ownership filtering. Eliminating the confident-wrong requires ownership; recovering a correct estimate additionally requires better ball-evidence disambiguation.

On committed real gold (n=15), ownership is NOT the limiting factor: even adversarially wrong ownership (other-player paddle points fed as target's, 7/15 events affected) produces zero confident-wrong markers and metrics identical to oracle ownership, because the paddle_track_beyond_reach tether (contact-evidence-4.x) excludes off-body paddle points regardless of claimed ownership.

Sparse oracle paddle points slightly HURT committed-gold replay: one previously correct estimate (wavea-944403-dink @21113ms, error 18ms, confidence 0.782 under current_no_paddle) becomes an abstention under oracle ownership, because 5 sparse in-window paddle points redirect ball-proximity gating (ball_never_near_target_paddle) away from the wrist gate. The estimator assumes dense paddle tracks; 1-10 annotation points per window are not a usable paddle modality.

The 3 wrong markers on committed gold (155/148/144ms, all confidence < 0.7) exist in the NO-paddle condition and are unchanged by any ownership condition: they are downstream contact-evidence localization error, not ownership error.
Current frame-level ownership accuracy on the dual-labeled set: 13/18 correct on the pose subset (1 abstention), 13/39 on all dual frames (22 abstentions, mostly missing pose).
rationale: The oracle question is answered with counts on the full in-scope evidence: perfect ownership eliminates the F09 confident-wrong residual on the adversarial fixtures (1 -> 0 of 12) by converting it to abstention, but does not recover correct localization on F3, and on all 15 replayable committed gold events ownership (perfect or adversarially wrong) changes no confident-wrong count (0 in all three conditions) because the existing reach tether already neutralizes foreign paddle tracks. Attribution: the confident-wrong failure mode is upstream (ownership), the residual localization ambiguity and the 3 low-confidence wrong markers are downstream (contact evidence). PROVISIONAL_GREEN rather than GREEN because Linux replay is non-canonical (no Mac/Apple Vision cascade), the F2/F3 scenarios are synthetic reconstructions, and committed paddle annotations are too sparse to emulate a real dense oracle paddle track.
environment: Linux replay only; no Swift/Mac/iPhone numbers claimed or fabricated.
